admission.justification: A disappearing cache file must not turn a harmless cleanup race into failed work, while a public orphan path must not publish or complete authority that has no master. The separate bounded guards prevent both failure classes without weakening identity checks.

applicability: Converted-base cache eviction and public leaf task-document/start/publication/finalization routes requiring master authority.
conditions: Eviction tolerates OSError while a listed old cache entry disappears before stat or unlink, without losing the newly stored usable entry.
Public leaf create/edit publication requires its master authority; low-level fixture/store writes do not supply a public orphan-creation exception.
A masterless public start/preview fails closed on source lineage, and missing leaf/master/row finalization fails before preparing completion publication.
Valid series-master finalization and existing master-plus-leaf planning remain distinct from the removed standalone-leaf fallback.
exclusions: Best-effort cache eviction is not an atomic cache transaction, blanket error suppression or a source-lineage waiver.
This proposes the source-backed obligation, not a concurrency/start/finalization test run, task write, Git transaction or acceptance.
statement: Cache eviction tolerates concurrent deletion and no public route creates, starts, publishes or finalizes a leaf without the required master authority.
